extracted.intended_audience: card issuers (banks and credit unions), industry trade associations, regulators, legal counsel, and other stakeholders responding to or implementing Regulation Z §1026.52
extracted.subtask_description: Section-by-section analysis and final rule decisions regarding limitations on penalty fees (especially late fees) under Regulation Z §1026.52, including safe-harbor amounts, cost-analysis provisions, applicability to 'Smaller Card Issuers', and related commentary/disclosure examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Smaller Card Issuer'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'Smaller Card Issuer' is defined to mean a card issuer that together with its affiliates had fewer than one million open credit card accounts as defined in §1026.58(b)(6) for the entire preceding calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB determined one million open accounts is an appropriate limit because comment letters highlighted concerns specific to such issuers; Smaller Card Issuers are not subject to certain proposed changes (notably the $8 late-fee safe harbor and elimination of annual adjustments) and will continue to be governed by the safe harbor thresholds in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(A)-(C) and the annual adjustment provisions in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(D). The CFPB explains the account-count metric better captures issuers with large card portfolios and economies of scale than using total assets or outstanding balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor late fee threshold ($8) for Larger Card Issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB adopted a new $8 late-fee safe harbor threshold applicable to card issuers other than 'Smaller Card Issuers' (i.e., Larger Card Issuers — those with one million or more open credit card accounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule lowers the safe harbor for late fees to $8 (from prior higher amounts) for Larger Card Issuers and removes the higher safe harbor for subsequent violations as it applies to late fees. CFPB expects this will apply to roughly the largest 30–35 issuers by outstanding balances and cover >95% of outstanding balances. The commentary and illustrative examples were revised to reflect $8 where applicable. The $8 threshold does not apply to Smaller Card Issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor vs. cost-analysis alternative (§1026.52(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A card issuer must not impose a fee for violating account terms unless the fee's dollar amount (1) represents a reasonable proportion of the total costs incurred for that type of violation as determined under the cost analysis provisions in §1026.52(b)(1)(i) or (2) complies with the safe harbor provisions in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty fees covered include late fees, returned-payment fees, and over-the-limit fees. Commentary (including illustrative examples in 52(b)(1)-1.i.B/C and 52(b)(1)-1.ii) explains the relationship between cost-analysis and safe-harbor approaches and was revised to reflect changes to the late-fee safe harbor (e.g., replacing late-fee examples with over-the-limit fees where late fees are being changed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost analysis provisions — permissible costs and reevaluation (§1026.52(b)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §1026.52(b)(1)(i), a card issuer may impose a penalty fee if the issuer determines the dollar amount represents a reasonable proportion of total costs incurred as a result of that type of violation; the issuer must reevaluate that determination at least once every 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB clarified in comment 52(b)(1)(i)-2.i that costs for purposes of cost analysis do NOT include collection costs incurred after an account is charged off in accordance with loan-loss provisions. Comment 52(b)(1)(i)-2 also lists other amounts not considered costs (e.g., losses and associated costs, holding reserves). CFPB solicited comment on the clarification and adopted it for all card issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on imposing a penalty fee that exceeds the dollar amount associated with the violation (§1026.52(b)(2)(i)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1026.52(b)(2)(i)(A) prohibits imposing a penalty fee that exceeds the dollar amount associated with the violation; current regulatory text prohibits late fees that exceed 100 percent of the required minimum payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition is an absolute constraint subject to the definitions of 'dollar amount associated with the violation' in the rule. CFPB proposed a change (see next entry) but did not finalize some of those proposed caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed 25 percent limitation on late fees (not finalized)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the 2023 Proposal, the CFPB proposed to amend §1026.52(b)(2)(i)(A) to provide that late fee amounts may not exceed 25 percent of the required minimum payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous commenters urged the CFPB to consider the disparate impact of a 25 percent limitation on credit unions and small issuers. CFPB did not finalize the 25 percent restriction for any card issuers (including Smaller Card Issuers) in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual adjustment of safe-harbor dollar amounts to reflect CPI (§1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: Current §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(D) provides for annual adjustments of safe-harbor dollar amounts to reflect changes in the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB proposed eliminating annual CPI adjustments for the late-fee safe harbor. In the final rule CFPB elected not to eliminate the annual adjustment for Smaller Card Issuers; it eliminated the annual adjustment for the late-fee safe harbor only for Larger Card Issuers (the $8 safe harbor). The CFPB explained the data used to compare collections costs to CPI relate to certain Larger Card Issuers (Y-14 issuers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic statement disclosure requirements for open-end plans (§1026.7(b)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1026.7(b)(11) requires that for a credit card account a card issuer must provide on each periodic statement: (1) the due date for a payment (same day each billing cycle), and (2) the amount of any late payment fee and any increased periodic rate(s) (expressed as APRs) that may be imposed as a result of a late payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment 7(b)(11)-4 allows a card issuer that imposes a range of late fees to state the highest fee with an indication that lower fees may be imposed (example language 'up to $29' previously). The CFPB amended the example to read 'up to $8' (to align with the $8 safe harbor for Larger Card Issuers) and adopted the change; CFPB noted the example is useful even though Smaller Card Issuers are not subject to the $8 safe harbor.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-year total fee cap (§1026.52(a)(1)) and excluded fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1026.52(a)(1) provides the total amount of fees a consumer is required to pay during the first year after account opening must not exceed 25 percent of the credit limit in effect when the account is opened. Section 1026.52(a)(2) excludes late payment fees, over-the-limit fees, returned-payment fees, and other fees that the consumer is not required to pay with respect to the account from that limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments illustrating the rule (comment 52(a)(1)-1.i and iv) contained late fee amounts; CFPB revised those examples to use $8 in the examples for entities that the $8 safe harbor applies to, while clarifying the examples show a card issuer that is not a Smaller Card Issuer. CFPB adopted minor technical cross-reference edits as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commentary and illustrative example revisions (clarifying definitions, rounding, and basis of dollar examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB revised commentary to §1026.52(b) (e.g., comment 52(b)-1.i.A, comment 52(b)-2, new comment 52(b)-5, and others) to clarify that a 'late payment fee' is any fee imposed for a late payment, to revise rounding examples to be consistent with the $8 late-fee safe harbor for Larger Card Issuers, and to explain the basis for dollar amounts used in commentary examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New comment 52(b)-5 clarifies that dollar-amount examples in the commentary are based on historical safe-harbor thresholds ($25 and $35 for penalty fees other than late fees) and the $8 threshold for late fees, and clarifies that $8 applies to card issuers other than Smaller Card Issuers. CFPB removed references to late fees in certain illustrative examples and replaced them with over-the-limit fees where appropriate to reflect the substantive changes to late-fee safe harbors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of account-count metric rather than total assets/outstandings for applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB chose to base the Smaller vs. Larger Card Issuer distinction on the number of open credit card accounts rather than on institution total asset size or amount of outstanding balances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: number of open accounts better captures issuers with large credit card portfolios and economies of scale similar to Y-14 issuers but that might not meet total-asset or outstanding-balance thresholds. This approach aligns with other Regulation Z provisions (e.g., exceptions for submitting card agreements under §1026.58). CFPB used public and confidential data to inform this choice.
